info.description: Staffing and capacity planning API for The Slot Finder
info.title: The Slot Finder API

get.description: Check if the service is running

delete.description: A person may remove their own absences; planners anyone's and holidays.
delete.summary: Remove an absence or a holiday

post.description: Turns a person's planned absence into an approved one and records an AbsenceAdded change event with the new status. An approved absence or a holiday gets ABSENCE_NOT_PLANNED.

get.description: Changes that may break the plan (absence, slipped phases and deadlines), newest first, with their processing status and re-plan draft. With program_id, only changes that touch its projects; the program page uses it for the re-plan banner.
Check if the database connection is healthy
Get detailed database connection metrics

post.description: Planners. Send an ICS file or an https link to a holiday calendar (a host in CALENDAR_ALLOWED_HOSTS), not both. Each event between from_date and to_date becomes a company holiday named after it; an event imported before is skipped. The link is never stored or logged.

get.description: Person × week load, capacity, utilization band and hours per expertise from the baseline. Weeks default to the current week and HEATMAP_DEFAULT_WEEKS; a range over HEATMAP_MAX_WEEKS gets WEEK_RANGE_TOO_LONG. With expertise, keeps people who hold it or work on it in the range. With program_id, keeps the people of that program's team; a manager may filter only by a program they may read.

parameters.description: Program id: only the people of its team
parameters.name: program_id

get.description: Open projects that are understaffed, at risk or behind on delivery, and people over 100 % in the next HEATMAP_DEFAULT_WEEKS weeks. A manager gets the projects of the programs they lead or lead a project in.
The signed-in user, read from the verified access token: id, username, name, email and role, plus person_id. On the first sign-in the person record is matched by email and linked to the account.
People ordered by name, each with their skills (primary first).

post.description: Creates a person with their expertise and levels. Exactly one expertise must be primary.

get.description: One person with their skills (primary first), for the person page.

patch.description: Changes only the fields sent. start_date and end_date accept null to clear them.

get.description: Leave and training of one person, oldest first. A person may read their own; planners anyone's.

post.description: Adds leave or training for a person (dates inclusive). A person may add their own, always as planned; planners may add anyone's and choose the status.

get.description: Assignments with hours from one ISO week through another. Specialists may read only their own.
The status of the person's connected calendar: host, last sync, last error and events found. Never the link.

put.description: Checks the secret iCal link (https, allowed host), syncs it once and stores it encrypted, replacing an earlier one.

delete.description: Removes the link. Absences it created stay, as ordinary absences.

post.description: Reads the calendar at once. A calendar that cannot be read keeps its absences and returns its error code in last_error.

get.description: Per ISO week: capacity, load, utilization band, tentative flag and hours per project from the baseline, computed as on the heatmap. Per working day: the person's absences and the company-wide holidays. A range over SCHEDULE_MAX_WEEKS gets WEEK_RANGE_TOO_LONG. Planners and leads may read anyone; others only themselves.

put.description: Replaces the person's whole expertise list. Exactly one must be primary; each expertise appears once.

patch.description: Moving end_week later by N weeks moves every later phase of the project by N weeks in the same transaction; moving it earlier moves nothing else. Returns every phase that changed.

get.description: The published plan in force, with every assignment and its weekly hours.
Every staffing draft that is still open, newest first, manual and auto re-plan. A manager (lead) sees only drafts whose projects all belong to programs they manage.
A manager gets the programs they lead or lead a project in.

post.description: Planners may set lead_id; a lead who creates a program becomes its lead.

get.description: A manager reaches only the programs they lead or lead a project in.

patch.description: Only the fields sent change. charter_url and lead_id accept null; only planners change the lead. status is rejected: use an action.

post.description: hold (open → pending), resume (pending → open), start-closing (open → closing), close (closing → closed), cancel (open, pending or closing → cancelled; also cancels its open projects).

get.description: Everyone with baseline hours on the program's projects, most hours first: hours per expertise and assignment kind, first and last week, and the projects. A manager reaches only the programs they lead or lead a project in.

Time, Scope, Planned burn and Staffing with their warnings, cost figures (budget, planned, forecast, gap, planned to date) and staffing by expertise, summed over projects that are not cancelled. A manager reaches only the programs they lead or lead a project in.

put.description: Planners and the program's manager. project_ids lists every project of the program, top first; their priorities become 1, 2, 3… in that order.
put.summary: Set the order of a program's projects

get.description: Projects by priority, then deadline, each with its current phase, at_risk and metrics (Time, Scope, Planned burn, Staffing). A manager reaches only the programs they lead or lead a project in.

post.description: Planners and the program's lead. The project starts as incoming.
post.summary: Add a project to a program

get.description: The people a planner gave the program, with their skills and their hours, weeks and projects in its baseline. The planner and the program's manager may read it.

post.description: Puts a person in the program's team, so its manager may staff them on its projects.

delete.description: Takes a person out of the program's team. Their baseline hours stay; the next draft plans without them.

get.description: Filter by status, e.g. ?status=incoming for the intake queue. A manager gets the projects of the programs they lead or lead a project in.
The project with its phases and demand; each demand lists the weeks it may be staffed in. A manager reaches only the programs they lead or lead a project in.

patch.description: Only the fields sent change, including scope_points and done_points. lead_id accepts null; only planners change the lead. status is rejected: use an action.

post.description: hold (incoming, planned or active → on_hold), resume (on_hold → incoming), complete (incoming, planned or active → done), cancel (any open status → cancelled).

put.description: The full list. Rows with an id are updated, without one added, missing ones removed. A row without phase_id spans the project's start week through its deadline week.
The full ordered list (its order is the sequence). Phases with an id are updated, without one added, missing ones removed; a phase that still has demand cannot be removed (409).

get.description: Every scenario, newest first, with its assumptions, churn and whether the baseline has moved on since.

post.description: Applies the assumptions (a project moving by weeks, a person away) to a copy of the baseline, plans the affected projects again and saves the result. Nothing else changes.

get.description: The scenario's assumptions, the projects planned again, and its changes, churn and unmet demand against the baseline it was built on.

post.description: Computes the scenario again, with the same assumptions, against the baseline in force.
The planning engine staffs the projects' demand on top of the baseline. Only incoming, planned or active projects.

get.description: The draft's assignments for the covered demand, coverage and unmet reasons, and changes against the baseline in force.

post.description: Publishes the draft as the new baseline, only while the baseline is still base_version (else 409 PLAN_VERSION_CONFLICT). Stretch assignments need confirm_stretch. Fully staffed incoming projects become planned.

patch.description: Add or remove assignments and change weekly hours or locks, all in one transaction. The server sets each added assignment's kind; a stretch assignment is locked.

get.description: Members of the demand's program team who hold its expertise at the required level and do not cover it yet, with the hours they have free over the demand's window, most first. At most DRAFT_ALTERNATIVES_LIMIT. To swap, send one remove and one add in the same PATCH of the draft's assignments.
get.summary: People who could take over an assignment

post.description: Upload a filled-in template as the multipart field "file". Every row is checked first: any problem saves nothing and returns 400 TIMESHEET_INVALID with data.problems [{line, column, code}]. A row with an empty actual_hours is skipped; importing again overwrites the same person, project and week. A file over TIMESHEET_MAX_BYTES or TIMESHEET_MAX_ROWS gets 413 TIMESHEET_TOO_LARGE. Records no change event.

get.description: A CSV with one row per person × project × week that has baseline or actual hours in the range, with planned hours and any actual hours already recorded. Weeks default to the TIMESHEET_TEMPLATE_WEEKS up to the current week; a week after the current one gets TIMESHEET_WEEK_IN_FUTURE and a range over TIMESHEET_MAX_WEEKS gets WEEK_RANGE_TOO_LONG.

name.description: Name says what a holiday is; empty for leave.

base_version.description: BaseVersion is the draft's base_version; a different baseline in force gives 409.

confirm_stretch.description: ConfirmStretch must be true when the draft has stretch assignments.

free_hours.description: FreeHours is the person's capacity minus the plan's hours over the demand's window.

reason.description: Reason says why their skill fits the demand, as a proposal words it.

by_hand.description: ByHand is true when a Planner added the assignment; false when the engine proposed it.

payload.description: Payload depends on the type, e.g. person_name, from_date and to_date for absence.

person_id.description: PersonID is the user's person record, or null when the account has none.

near_full_from.description: NearFullFrom: from this share up to 100 % the week is near full; over 100 % it is overloaded.

underused_below.description: UnderusedBelow: under this share of capacity the week is underused.

team_ids.description: TeamIDs are the people of the program team who may staff the demand; null puts no limit.

unmet_reason.description: UnmetReason is the engine's code for hours it could not place when it made the draft.

program_lead_id.description: ProgramLeadID is the person who manages the program; they may act on a draft of its projects.

assignments.description: Assignments are those of the covered demand; the rest of the baseline is unchanged.

auto.description: Auto is true for a re-plan draft that change events created; TriggeredBy lists them.

bands.description:
Bands are the limits for colouring a week; the client adds the hours of the cell it edits to
OtherHours of the person's weeks in Load.

base_version.description: BaseVersion is the baseline version the draft was built on; send it back to accept.

current_version.description: CurrentVersion is the baseline in force now. Stale is true when they differ.

load.description: Load lists every active person's capacity and other hours for each week the draft spans.

superseded_by.description: SupersededBy is the newer version of a re-plan draft that replaced this one.

capacity.description: Capacity is the person's bookable hours that week.

other_hours.description: OtherHours are the hours the plan gives the person on demand this draft does not cover.

primary.description: Primary is true when it is the person's primary skill.

actual_hours.description:
ActualHours is what the person worked that week from imported timesheets; null when
nothing was imported. Load, utilization and band stay planned.

tentative.description: Tentative marks planned (not yet approved) absence in the week.

utilization.description: Utilization is load ÷ capacity; null when capacity is 0.

auto.description: Auto is true for a re-plan draft that change events created.

base_version.description: BaseVersion is the baseline version the draft was built on; Stale is true when the baseline in force differs.

unmet_count.description: UnmetCount is how many demands the engine could not cover when the draft was generated.

projects.description: Projects is how many projects (not cancelled) the figures sum over.

actual_hours.description: ActualHours and BurnPercent are null until timesheets recorded actual hours.

next_week_hours.description:
NextWeekHours and NextThreeWeeksHours are the baseline hours in the week after the current
one, and in the three weeks after it.

metrics.description: Metrics is set on a program's project list: Time, Scope, Planned burn and Staffing.

program_lead_id.description: ProgramLeadID is the person who manages the program, when the program is loaded.

staffed_at.description: StaffedAt is when an accepted staffing draft first covered the whole project.

metrics.description: Metrics is set on a program's project list: Time, Scope, Planned burn and Staffing.

program_lead_id.description: ProgramLeadID is the person who manages the program, when the program is loaded.

staffed_at.description: StaffedAt is when an accepted staffing draft first covered the whole project.

retry_after.description: RetryAfter is in whole seconds, as in the Retry-After header.

before_from.description: The weeks are the first and last with hours; empty when there are none.

moved_hours.description: MovedHours is the hours placed in a week beyond what that week had before.

base_version.description:
BaseVersion is the baseline version it was computed on; Stale is true once the baseline
in force (CurrentVersion) is another one.

BaseVersion is the baseline version it was computed on; Stale is true once the baseline
in force (CurrentVersion) is another one.

hours_moved.description: HoursMoved is the hours placed in a week beyond what that week had in the baseline.

days.description: Days holds only the working days with an absence or a holiday.

working_weekdays.description: WorkingWeekdays are ISO day numbers: 1 is Monday, 7 is Sunday.

actual_hours.description: ActualHours is null until a timesheet import recorded hours for the week.

tentative.description: Tentative marks planned (not yet approved) absence in the week.

utilization.description: Utilization is load ÷ capacity; null when capacity is 0.

locked.description: Locked pins the week; leave it out to keep the current lock.

BearerAuth.description: Bearer Token Authentication. Use "Bearer {token}" as the value.
BearerAuth.name: Authorization
